newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Philips says Asia key as Europe stumbles.
newsitem.headline: Philips says Asia key as Europe stumbles.

text.p: Philips Electronics NV said on Thursday its businesses in Asia continued to be the mainstay of its lower operating income in the first nine months of 1996.

Announcing a plunge in third quarter net profit from normal operations to 123 million guilders from 539 million and to 804 million from 1.7 billion in the first nine months, finance director Dudley Eustace highlighted the Asia performance.
"Almost two thirds of our income from operations was earned in the Asia Pacific region, on 20 pecent of our sales. Last year some 36 percent on 20 percent of our sales," he said.

"The story is a sad one for Europe and North America where price pressures are at their strongest and demand at its weakest. The solution can only come from increased pressure on costs which ultimately leads to fewer jobs," he said, referring to an earlier announced proposed fourth quarter charge of one billion guilders.
Income from operations at the group slumped to 281 million guilders in the third quarter from a previous 922 million and to 1.5 billion from 2.8 billion for the nine months.
Price pressures bit into every division of the company, Eustace told reporters.
"In the first nine months of 1995, price pressure was two percent on average, that doubled to four percent in 1996," said Eustace.
Income from operations in the January to September period in Asia climbed to 968 million guilders from a previous 843 million guilders.
In Europe nine month operating income slid to 274 million guilders from 1.35 billion and in North America to 33 million from 353 million.
Eustace said the most dramatic year on year development was in the semiconductor industry, with price erosion in Philips' case increasing from two percent in 1995 to eight percent in 1996.

"In such a business as semiconductors with very high fixed costs, most of the price deterioration falls straight through to the bottom line. The business is still very attractive but relative to 1995, considerably less so," Eustace said.
